correctness.rationale: For all compact positive-area planar convex Q and all h>0, direct Minkowski projection geometry gives brightness B=A Z+h sqrt(1−Z²)w_Q(V), where Z is uniform [0,1] independently of uniform azimuth V. Five elementary spherical beta integrals imply the exact quadratic variance; positive leading coefficient g+2s/3 and negative linear coefficient yield a unique positive optimizer. Width variance s≥0 with equality iff continuous width function constant, giving sharp universal bound and exact gap. For equality cases B/A has exact pushforward law Z+t sqrt(1−Z²); solving the quadratic equation for Z gives piecewise CDF. Checker ran from actual package directory with VERIFY_OK and independently agrees with known orthotope moments; finite quadrature is not proof.

value.rationale: The right-prism class is natural and infinite dimensional in its planar bases; selecting its height to minimize random-view shadow-area dispersion solves an intrinsic shape-versus-aspect optimization. It identifies all noncircular constant-width bases as sharp equalizers, exactly characterizes width-anisotropy penalty, and proves all optimal equalizers have the same entire area-normalized shadow law. These structural relations cannot be inferred from a finite cube table, and support geometric sensing and random-projection stability comparisons; they are more than a routine single-body moment computation.
